answer: Every boat that leaves the harbor carries a small argument with the sea. Mine was a cheap rowboat, and on the third morning a gale came down the channel fast enough to turn the water white. I learned then that a ripple is not a small wave; it is a rumor of one, passed hand to hand until the whole surface agrees. Steering into it felt less like courage than arithmetic: one stroke, then another, until the count beat the fear. By dusk I reached the far shore, where a single rock rose to a sharp vertex above the tide line. I tied off and sat still, listening to the wind forget me.
